newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-FINANCE MINISTER STEPS INTO 1860 MUNICH ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FINANCE MINISTER STEPS INTO 1860 MUNICH ROW.

text.p: A bizarre dispute at Bundesliga side 1860 Munich took an even more unusual turn on Monday when German Finance Minister Theo Waigel stepped into the row.
Waigel, one of 1860's most prominent fans, threw his weight behind midfielder Manfred Schwabl, stripped of the club captaincy for not turning up to an official end-of-season party.
The soccer-mad minister said he would take up Schwabl's case with club president Karlheinz Wildmoser and coach Werner Lorant.
"What's happened recently is a shame. Manni Schwabl is a real ambassador for 1860," Waigel told the Bild daily. "My stance is clearly pro Schwabl."
Schwabl has been told he will not play for the club again after what the German media have dubbed the "party affair".
The trouble began after the 31-year-old organised a party for the players but Wildmoser later announced an end-of-season club function for the same night.
Schawabl and another player did not turn up at all to the club party and the rest of the squad left after early to join the function organised by the captain.
"I've been made a victim in order to discipline the team," Schwabl declared in an interview with Kicker magazine on Monday.
